articles.headline: Watch-Meeting (editorial: Bethel watch-night; Recorder visit to the A. M. E. Union Church)
articles.summary: On last Saturday night this most impressive and solemn feature of Christian worship was observed by many of our churches within the city. We were present at Bethel Church, watching with the brethren for the death of the Old Year and the birth of the New.

articles.headline: City Notices (holiday fairs: Bethel, St. Thomas', Hurst Street, Wesley, Union)
articles.summary: During the holidays there was a perfect and almost endless round of Fairs, Festivals, Suppers and social evening parties within the limits of our own fair city of Brotherly Love.

articles.headline: Lecture at Bethel Church by Mrs. F. E. W. Harper, 'The Mission of the War'
articles.summary: At Bethel Church, on the 28th ultimo, by Mrs. F. E. W. Harper. This much renowned lecturer is so well known amongst the community for her ability as a public speaker, that any eulogy by us might seem superfluous.

articles.headline: Bethel Sabbath School (Christmas celebration)
articles.summary: For some years it has been the custom for the above-named Sabbath School to celebrate the birth-day of our blessed Saviour.
people: speaker; formerly an officer of the Bethel Sabbath School (Esq.)

articles.headline: Indianapolis Correspondence (acknowledges gift from H. Gordon of Philadelphia)
articles.author: W. R. Revels
articles.summary: For some three weeks past we have been enjoying a gracious revival of the religion of the blessed Lord in our charge in this place. Thirty have been happily converted to God.
people: of Philadelphia; donor of two dollars toward the Indianapolis church building

articles.headline: Letter from A. W. Wayman on his New York, New Jersey and Philadelphia district tour
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: Travel letter of Rev. A. W. Wayman, dated Baltimore, December 27th, 1864, reporting visits to churches in New York State, New Jersey and Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Interesting Lectures!! (S. C. and Statistical Association course at Concert Hall; proceeds toward streetcar rights)
articles.summary: A course of Six Lectures will be given, this Winter, at Concert Hall, under the auspices of the S. C. and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania. William Lloyd Garrison will deliver the opening lecture, on Monday evening, January 16th.

articles.headline: Grand Public Demonstration (Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League ovation to Rev. Calvin Fairbank)
articles.summary: The Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League will tender to the great sufferer in the cause of human freedom and the advancement of equal rights, the Rev. Calvin Fairbank, a grand public ovation, in 'honor to whom honor is due,' at National Hall, Market street, above Twelfth, on Wednesday evening, January 11th, 1865.

articles.headline: Grand Lodge for the State of Pennsylvania (installation of officers, Dec. 27, 1864)
articles.summary: At the annual grand communication, (St. John, the Evangelist's day,) held in their hall, South Eleventh Street, Philadelphia, December 27th, A. D., 1864, A. L. 5864, the following named brethren, having been elected December 5th, 1864, for the ensuing masonic year, were this day duly installed.

articles.headline: A Grand Concert and festival at Odd Fellows Hall for the A. M. E. Church at Frankford
articles.summary: And festival will be given at Odd Fellows Hall, on Thursday evening, 12th inst., for the benefit of the A. M. E. Church at Frankford. Several distinguished speakers will address the assembly. Cars leave Sixth and Powell at 5 1/2 and 6 P. M., return at 11 o'clock.

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly Meetings of Horntown Circuit (Chester, Pa.)
articles.author: E. Weaver
articles.summary: Quarterly Conference at Chester, Pa., at 3 P. M., on Saturday, 14th. Quarterly meeting on the 15th, and Jubilee the same day. At Horntown, the Quarterly meeting will be on the 22d.

articles.headline: Notice: Home for Aged and Infirm Colored People, first annual meeting of contributors
articles.author: M. Balderston
articles.summary: The first Annual Meeting of the contributors to the Home, will be held on Thursday evening, the 12th inst., at 8 o'clock, in the West room of National Hall, Market St. above 12th, 2d story.

articles.headline: Notice: J. Anderson Raymond lecture at Scott's Union Baptist church, Minster street
articles.summary: J. Anderson Raymond will lecture at Scott's Union Baptist church, Minster street, on Thursday evening, January 12th, 1865. Subject, 'Africa and her People: their rights and wrongs considered, and their future prosperity.' Proceeds to be devoted to the benefit of Sabbath School of said church.

articles.headline: The National League (address of the Executive Board, National Equal Rights League)
articles.author: John M. Langston
articles.summary: To the Colored People of the United States: At our late National Convention, held in Syracuse, N. Y., we formed a National Equal Rights' League.

articles.headline: Appeal to the Colored People of the State of Pennsylvania; Preamble and Constitution and officers of the Equal Rights League of the State of Pennsylvania
articles.summary: Fellow Citizens: You have learned through your delegates, as well as through the published proceedings of the late National Convention, held at Syracuse, N. Y., that a National Equal Rights' League has been organized.

articles.headline: Married (James W. Brown and Emily E. Effer; Wm. H. Gaston and Eliza Greenwich)
articles.summary: At the residence of the bride, Monday the 26th inst., by the Rev. J. P. Davenport, rector of St. Ann's Protestant Episcopal Church, Miss Emily E. Effer, eldest daughter of the late Benjamin Effer, Esq., of Annapolis, Md., to Mr. James W. Brown, of Philadelphia, formerly of Baltimore, Md.
people: groom; of Philadelphia, formerly of Baltimore
bride, of Annapolis (printed Effer here; corrected Jan 14 to Emily E. Offer)
officiating minister (Rev.), Philadelphia wedding of Jan. 2, 1865

articles.headline: James O. Clark, M. D. (Eclectic), No. 618 Pine Street
articles.summary: James O. Clark, M. D. (Eclectic.) No. 618 Pine Street, Philadelphia. Office hours ... Also, particular attention directed to all classes of Ulcers, recent or chronic. Treatment and cure, without the use of Mercury, or any other injurious drug, warranted.

articles.headline: Cupping, Leeching & Bleeding attended to by Nathaniel L. Durham, 911 1/2 Christian Street
articles.summary: Cupping, Leeching & Bleeding attended to by Nathaniel L. Durham, 911 1/2 Christian Street. Also Agent and Solicitor for 'Security Life Insurance Company.'
people: cupper and leecher; insurance agent, 911 1/2 Christian Street

articles.headline: Coal Yard, Thos. J. Bowers, 634 Lombard Street above Sixth
articles.summary: Coal Yard. Thos. J. Bowers, (At 634 Lombard Street, above Sixth, Phila.,) has constantly on hand the best Lehigh, Schuylkill and other Coal, at the Lowest Market Price. Orders received at No. 115 South Second Street.
people: coal dealer, 634 Lombard Street above Sixth

articles.headline: W. R. Decordover's Periodical Depot, 419 South Seventh Street
articles.summary: W. R. Decordover's Periodical Depot, 419 South Seventh Street, Philada. Daily and Weekly papers always on hand. New York Ledger, Anglo-African, Harper's Weekly, &c., for sale. Also, Stationery.

articles.headline: Continental Restaurant, Charles W. Brister, No. 717 Lombard Street (proprietor reading)
articles.summary: Charles W. Brister, Continental Restaurant, No. 717 Lombard Street, Phila., (Above Seventh St., under Philadelphia Institute,) Where he continues to keep always on hand the very best assortment of Oysters and other refreshments. Meals served at all hours. Also, public and private waiting done on the most reasonable terms.

articles.headline: Letter from West Chester (Aid Society fair and supper for a new church)
articles.author: E. A. C.
articles.summary: West Chester, January 6th, 1865. Mr. Editor: With us the Christmas holidays have just past, and we had a glorious time. The ladies of the Aid Society, of West Chester, some six weeks before Christmas, formed a resolution to hold a fair, for the purpose of raising means to build a new church.
people: delivered an address on Love and Charity (Rev.)

articles.headline: A Good Time at Media (quarterly meeting, Rev. E. Laws's circuit)
articles.summary: On Saturday and Sabbath last, quarterly meeting was held at Media, Pa., by Rev. E. Laws. We had a very pleasant time there throughout the Sabbath day, notwithstanding the inclement weather.

articles.headline: The Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia
articles.summary: This Society has been very active in raising funds to help the sick and wounded soldiers. They are still at work, and apparently untiring in their efforts. We refer our readers to their advertisement, which will be found in another place in our paper.

articles.headline: A Word to our Brethren and Readers (list of agents and new subscribers to Jan. 10, 1865)
articles.summary: Some time ago, we promised to publish the number of new subscribers our brethren, agents and friends would send us by the 10th day of January, 1865. That day has passed, and we lay before our readers the result of the effort.
people: Recorder agent, Norristown (Rev.); printed 'W. R. Norris' in the text

articles.headline: Wm. Lloyd Garrison (opening lecture of the Social, Civil and Statistical Association course)
articles.summary: This tried friend of equality and the advancement of our race, will deliver the first of a course of lectures, to be given under the auspices of the Social, Civil, and Statistical Association, of colored people of Pennsylvania, at Concert Hall, Chestnut St., on Monday evening, 16th inst., at 8 o'clock.

articles.headline: Thanks (to Mr. Gleaves for oysters; puff for Mrs. Gleaves's trimming store, Pine street)
articles.summary: We take the present opportunity of returning our thanks to our esteemed friend, Mr. Gleaves, of this city, for the large and splendid lot of excellent Oysters which he kindly sent us. They were sent to him from old Virginia.

articles.headline: Married (correction: Emily E. Offer, bride of James W. Brown)
articles.summary: In our last issue, in noticing the marriage of our firm friend and active business man, Mr. James W. Brown, to Miss Emily E. Offer, of Annapolis, Md., on the 26th ult., there was, unfortunately, a typographical error. The name of the bride was incorrectly printed Emily O. Offer, instead of Emily E. Offer.
people: groom; 'our firm friend and active business man'

articles.headline: Notice: report of the ovation at National Hall next week
articles.summary: Report of the Ovation at National Hall will appear next week.

articles.headline: Letter from Calvin Fairbank (thanks for the Philadelphia reception at National Hall)
articles.author: Calvin Fairbank
articles.summary: Philadelphia, Pa., January 17, 1865. Mr. Editor: My soul is stirred to its depths by the realization of more than all my long-suspended anticipations of the dawn of Democracy.

articles.headline: To My Numerous Good Friends, in the Philadelphia and New England Districts, and Generally
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: I wish you all a Happy New Year. Providence permitting, I shall converse with you before long. So, good-by.

articles.headline: Rev. Sella Martin (second lecture of the Social, Civil, and Statistical Association course)
articles.summary: This truly eloquent and pulpit orator, and lecturer, will deliver the second of a course of lectures before the Social, Civil, and Statistical Association of the colored people of Pennsylvania, in Concert Hall, Wednesday evening next, Jan. 25th. Subject, 'The friends of the Union in England.'

articles.headline: Letter from Camden on emancipation in Maryland
articles.author: A. B.
articles.summary: Dear Editor: I write a few lines for you, hoping they may have room in your worthy columns. I wish to say a few words in relation to the emancipation in Maryland.

articles.headline: The Railway Suit for Damages: Charge of Judge Sawyer (William Bowen vs. North Beach and Mission Railroad, San Francisco)
articles.summary: Wm. Bowen vs. The North Beach and Mission Railroad Company: Gentlemen of the Jury: The plaintiff claims that on or about the 23d day of May, 1863, he was desirous to be carried on one of defendant's cars from California street to Mission St., and for that purpose stepped on to the rear platform of said car, and tendered to the conductor ten cents for his fare.

articles.headline: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights' League: Sergeant-Major A. M. Green's canvassing tour for the Harrisburg convention
articles.author: Jonathan C. Gibbs
articles.summary: Sergeant-Major A. M. Green, who has been one of the Solicitors and General Agent for the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights' League, will visit Pittsburg, Brownsville, Hollidaysburg, Altoona, Harrisburg, and intermediate places, with a view to rallying the friends of equal rights, in response to the call for a State Convention of the colored people of Pennsylvania, to convene at Harrisburg, on Wednesday, February 8th, 1865.
people: Sergeant-Major; solicitor and general agent of the League

articles.headline: An Obituary (Sister Emeline Jackson of Wesley Church, Hurst Street)
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: A discourse was delivered in the A. M. E. Wesley Church, in Hurst Street, Philadelphia, by Revs. H. Davis and J. H. Smith, on the 1st of January, 1865, from the 23d Psalm. The discourse was called forth by the death of Sister Emeline Jackson.
people: deceased; member of Wesley A. M. E. Church, Hurst St., formerly of Zion A. M. E., Lombard St.

articles.headline: An Appeal: Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia, fair for sick and wounded colored soldiers
articles.summary: The Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia intend giving another fair for the sick and wounded colored soldiers. Feeling that the wants of the soldiers should be attended to by those for whom they are suffering every privation, and doing deeds of valor, we once again earnestly call on the public for assistance.
people: committee, N. E. cor. 11th and Race

articles.headline: Married (Brown and Weddon; Brush and Wheeler; Renson and Williams) and correction of the Easton marriage
articles.summary: BROWN and WEDDON. On the 12th day of January, by the Rev. Jas. Hamilton, Mr. Lewis Brown, of Clark County, Va., to Miss Susan Weddon, of the same place.

articles.headline: Obituary (Mrs. Mary Ann Hatton; Lottie Cowdery)
articles.summary: Died. In the city of Philadelphia, December 17th, Mrs. Mary Ann Hatton, in the fifty-sixth year of her age, a native of Washington Co., Ind.
people: brother of the deceased Lottie Cowdery

articles.headline: Military Instruction given to Companies, Associations, &c. (James J. Spelman)
articles.summary: Military Instruction given to Companies, Associations, &c. Terms Moderate. Address James J. Spelman, South Street, Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights Convention (call to Harrisburg)
articles.author: Jonathan C. Gibbs
articles.summary: Elective Franchise, Colored Commissioned Officers, Equal Public Schools. A Convention will be held in Harrisburg, on the second Wednesday in February, 1865, at 10 o'clock, A. M., in accordance with the order of the National Convention held at Syracuse, New York, Oct. 4, 1864.

articles.headline: Judge Kelley's Great Speech in the House of Representatives (and the assault on him by A. P. Field)
articles.summary: The Speech of Mr. Kelley is one of the most masterly ever delivered in the House on the constitutional question of amending the Constitution of the United States. We have read the Judge's speech with no little degree of interest.

articles.headline: The Right of Colored People to Ride in the Cars (introducing Senator Morrow B. Lowry's speech)
articles.summary: We give place this week to the insertion of the great and humane speech of the Hon. Morrow B. Lowry, delivered in the Senate of Pennsylvania, on the 10th of January, 1865. We do this, in order that the colored people of this country may, in future, know who are their real friends.

articles.headline: State Equal Rights Convention (Philadelphia meeting at Franklin Hall to elect delegates to Harrisburg)
articles.summary: Last evening, in pursuance of a call issued by the Executive Board, a meeting assembled in Franklin Hall, to make arrangements for having Philadelphia fully represented in the State Equal Rights Convention, which assembles in Harrisburg, February 8th.

articles.headline: A Soldier's Letter from near Richmond (43d U. S. C. T.)
articles.author: Henry C. Hoyle
articles.summary: Near Richmond, Va., Jan. 10th, 1865. Mr. Editor: Having a few leisure moments I take the opportunity to address a few lines to you to inform you how we are getting along. All is quiet along our lines.

articles.headline: From the Front: letter of a private of the 43d U. S. C. T. on officers striking soldiers
articles.summary: Bermuda Hundred, Va. Dear Editor: All is quiet along our lines, excepting a little picket firing, which has been kept up very briskly for three or four days.

articles.headline: Notice: ordination of five deacons at the Union Baptist Church, Minster Street (largely illegible)
articles.summary: There will be an ordination of five Deacons in the Union Baptist Church, Minster Street, on next Sabbath afternoon. Rev. J. D. M... will preach... (remainder illegible on the film).

articles.headline: National Equal Rights League (letter of Pittsburgh delegates to John M. Langston)
articles.author: George B. Vashon
articles.summary: To you, in your capacity as President of the National Equal Rights League, we, the delegates of the city of Pittsburg, Pa., to the recent National Convention of colored men at Syracuse, N.Y., would respectfully express our opinions in reference to the formation of bodies auxiliary to the said National League... We are induced to do this in view of a call for a State Convention emanating from the State Equal Rights' League of Pennsylvania.

articles.headline: Glorious News: Slavery Abolished from the Constitution (editorial)
articles.summary: We have the pleasure of chronicling in this issue of our paper, for the benefit of our readers, the thrilling and joyous intelligence that on the last day of January, 1865, the House of Representatives of the United States voted to amend the Constitution... This was carried by a vote of 119 for the amendment, to 56 in opposition to it.

articles.headline: An Important Letter from a Chaplain (25th U.S.C.T., Fort Barrancas)
articles.author: Enoch K. Miller
articles.summary: This has been something of a day of rejoicing with us, on account of the arrival of the mail. We have been deprived for a whole month of the privilege of home communication... Since writing, last month, we have had but four deaths in the regiment.
people: deceased; Co. K, 25th U.S.C.T.; died in the hospital in Philadelphia, November [22d or 23d]

articles.headline: Letter to the Bishops proposing a day of thanksgiving on March 4 (Harrisburg pastors)
articles.summary: To the Right Rev'd Superintendents and Bishops of the A.M.E. Zion, and A.M.E. Churches, To the Rev'd H. H. Garnet, of Washington, D. C., J. Sella Martin, of New York, Grimes, of Boston, and all good and true men, leaders and representatives of our race. Each day brings fresh evidence before us of the final disinthralment of slavery... we would also suggest a day to be set apart on the 4th day of March next, the day that President Lincoln renews his vows.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (subscription receipts)
articles.summary: Washington, D.C., per Rev. J. D. S. Hall, Mrs. Fletcher, $2.50... Darby, Pa., per Mrs. E. Harris, C. W. Hopkins, 1.00; Fanny Evans, 75 cts.

articles.headline: Substitute Wanted (homestead in Norristown offered)
articles.summary: A Homestead will be given to any man who will serve as a substitute for three years in the army. It consists of a three-story house, (six rooms,) and lot of ground, with hydrant and all modern conveniences; is situated in the borough of Norristown, Penna., and clear of all incumbrances. Any application can be made to Leizeare [VERIFY] Brown, 907 South Street, Philadelphia, Pa.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (subscription receipts)
articles.summary: Spring Dale, Iowa, Mrs. A. L. Ralley per B. F. Taylor, $2.50... West Phila., Rev. B. Berry, for Benjamin Carpenter, 1.00. Camden, N.J., Rev. T. G. Steward, for Eliza Fisher, 2.75... Mount Holly, N.J., Julia Waterman, Chas. Sabey, and Martha Gaines, each 2.50. Burlington, N.J., Chas. Williams, 2.50; Wm. Thomas, 5.00; Mary Mitchell, 1.00. Germantown, Pa., Sarah Hubert, 2.50.

articles.headline: Obituary verses for Ann F. Bristol, Attleborough
articles.author: L. H. O.
articles.summary: Thou wast mild and lovely. Dearest Ann, mild and lovely, Pleasant as the summer breeze... The above touching verses I respectfully dedicate to the memory of our departed friend, Ann F. Bristol [VERIFY]. L. H. O. Attleborough, Jan. 18th, 1865.

articles.headline: Married (Hodges-Parker; Hamilton-Hatton)
articles.summary: HAMILTON-HATTON. On Jan. 17th, 1865, by Rev. Jeremiah Asher, Mark [VERIFY] Hamilton to Miss [illegible] Hatton [VERIFY]. HODGES-PARKER. On Thursday evening, Feb. 2d, by Rev. Stephen Smith, Wilson Hodges to Mary E. Parker. All of this city.

articles.headline: Letter from 25th U.S.C.T. (Company K, camp near Barrancas)
articles.summary: I have come to the conclusion that I would try my hand for the first time, to address you a few lines for your columns... My company, (K.) the most unlucky company of the regiment, has not been with the regiment since last May... When we left camp William Penn, Phila., it numbered 90 men, but sickness has reduced it to 65.
people: deceased; Co. K, 25th U.S.C.T.; 'said to be an old citizen of Philadelphia'; found dead in his bed at Gunboat Point, Fla.

articles.headline: Negro Suffrage (editorial on the Philadelphia Inquirer)
articles.summary: We were astonished to find in the editorial columns of the Philadelphia Inquirer of the 14th instant a letter inserted under the pretence of a communication, in relation to negro suffrage... Can any rational man... have the effrontery to undertake to say that it is right to exclude any man from public conveyance on account of color?

articles.headline: Frankford and Southwark Horse Railroad experiment (editorial on the Public Ledger)
articles.summary: The Public Ledger (Philadelphia) says that the Frankford and Southwark Horse Railroad has tried the experiment of letting colored persons ride in its cars, and found it unprofitable, more being lost by whites refusing to ride with negroes than is gained by the custom of the latter... We have only to say to Mr. Childs, the present editor and proprietor of The Ledger, that that is just what is the matter.

articles.headline: Died: Mrs. Sarah Ash
articles.summary: Mrs. Sarah Ash, one of our oldest citizens of color, and a noted Shrouder, departed this life on the 28th ultimo, aged 69 years. Mrs. Ash was one among the first who joined Bethel church; but at the time of the unhappy division, was one of those who went off with a party called the 'Israelites.' ... Her death was caused by typhoid fever.
people: deceased Jan. 28, 1865, aged 69 [VERIFY age 69/60]; shrouder; early member of Bethel, later with the 'Israelites'

articles.headline: Something New: Mrs. Julia C. Collins's narrative 'The Curse of Caste' announced
articles.summary: Mrs. Julia C. Collins, now of Williamsport, Pennsylvania, proposes to write a narrative on the Curse of Cast, through the columns of The Recorder, and as we go to press we have received the commencement, the first chapter, which will appear next week.

articles.headline: A Blunder, and Who Made It (Germantown church letter correction)
articles.author: P. Gardiner
articles.summary: In perusing the last issue of The Christian Recorder, I perceive you have committed several errors in the extract from my letter... The condition of the Church at Germantown does not convey the desired idea, by being wrongly punctuated... 'This year they have paid the carpenter, and all other demands.'

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (subscription receipts)
articles.summary: Clearfield, Md., Rev. E. Caution, for books, $7.75... West Chester, Rev. E. Laws, for Mrs. M. Hutchinson, 2.50... Freehold, N.J., Rev. [?] Davis, for Mrs. Hendrickson, 2.50... Port Hudson, La., Rev. P. Read, Chaplain 76th U.S.C.I., for 20 subscribers, 50.00.

articles.headline: National Equal Rights League: Executive Board to meet in Philadelphia
articles.author: John M. Langston
articles.summary: All the members of the Executive Board are earnestly requested to meet in Philadelphia, March 10th, at 10 o'clock. Business of vital importance demands punctual attendance. By order of the President. John M. Langston, Pres't. Geo. B. Taylor, David D. Turner, Secretaries.

articles.headline: Obituary: Eliza Ann Davis, Evesham
articles.summary: Died at the residence of her parents, Eliza Ann Davis, in the 23d year of her age, oldest daughter of Robert and Sarah Anna Davis. She embraced religion at an early age. She was a faithful member of the A.M.E. Church at Evesham... She was a faithful Sabbath School teacher... Her charge was the infant class.
people: deceased, aged 22; Sabbath-school teacher, A.M.E. Church, Evesham, N.J.

articles.headline: Notice: Lebanon Cemetery (lot holders to pay J. C. White, Secretary)
articles.author: J. Asher
articles.summary: All those persons who have purchased lots in the Lebanon Cemetery, and have not as yet received the necessary deeds, will please call upon Mr. J. C. White, the Secretary, as he is hereby authorized to receive payment in part or in full. He will also answer every inquiry concerning the grounds. Full satisfaction will be given in the whole matter. (Signed) J. Asher.
people: secretary, Lebanon Cemetery (printed 'J. C. White'; the father, per Michiko 2026-11-11)

articles.headline: Negro Suffrage: 'A Reply' by 'Another American' (reprinted from the Evening Bulletin)
articles.author: Another American
articles.summary: We give place this week to a well-timed article on Negro Suffrage, from the 'Evening Bulletin' of the 17th inst., in answer to the opprobrious article in the Inquirer, of the 14th inst... As in Inquirer of to-day (14 inst.,) there appeared the communication upon the question of negro suffrage, fairness will not permit you to decline the publication of an adverse exposition of the subject.

articles.headline: Bordentown Circuit: Christian Commission collection acknowledged
articles.summary: We republish, for the satisfaction of the parties on the above named circuit, our acknowledgment of $55, collected for the Christian Commission in last December, in answer to our appeal to the various Churches... The same was sent to us by Rev. Mullen, through Brother Green.

articles.headline: The Pennsylvania Equal Rights League convention at Harrisburg (editorial)
articles.summary: We wish to say that, taking into consideration all the Conventions held by the colored people at which we had the pleasure and honor of being present, we doubt whether any previous one displayed a greater array of talent than the State Convention recently held at Harrisburg... not only the young and talented men of Philadelphia, but many from the country and surrounding villages, were present.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (subscription receipts)
articles.summary: Knoxville, Tenn., S. Lowery, for Mr. A. Lowery, 1.00... Thornbury, Pa., Rachel A. Brown, 1.25... Kingston, N.J., Rev. H. Davis, for John Raddle, 2.53...

articles.headline: Notice: Wilberforce address at Mount Pisgah A.M.E. Church, Princeton, N.J.
articles.author: H. Davis
articles.summary: There being no preventing Providence, there will be an address delivered in the A.M.E. Mount Pisgah Church, in Princeton, N.J., to the Sabbath school of said church, on the first Sabbath in March, at 3 o'clock, P.M., by the Elder, after which there will be a collection taken up in behalf of the Wilberforce University, in Xenia, Ohio... H. Davis, Pastor. February 20th, 1865.

articles.headline: Mrs. F. E. Watkins Harper lecture notice (Social, Civil and Statistical Association)
articles.author: Wm. Still
articles.summary: Mrs. F. E. Watkins Harper will deliver the Fourth Lecture of the Course before the Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the colored people of Pennsylvania, on Monday evening, February 27th, in Concert Hall. Subject: 'The Causes and Effects of the War.' Miss E. T. Greenfield, the celebrated 'Black Swan', and the Post band from Camp Wm. Penn, will perform.

articles.headline: Obituary: Mrs. Mary Robinson, Colored Women's Lincoln Association
articles.summary: Philadelphia, Feb. 6, 1865. At a special meeting of the Colored Women's Lincoln Association, auxiliary to the Sanitary Commission, the President announced the death of Mrs. Mary Robinson, one of the Board of Directors of the Association, when on motion Eliza Galloway, Sarah Ryder, Margaret Williams, Annie Gross, were appointed a committee to prepare a preamble and resolutions.
people: deceased; board of directors, Colored Women's Lincoln Association; left a husband and children

articles.headline: Married (Burlington, N.J.: Hogans-Davis; Williams-Romeo)
articles.summary: In Burlington, Feb. 14, by Rev. Theo. Gould, Miss Mary Louisa Davis, daughter of the Rev. Henry Davis, to Mr. Charles Hogans, of New York. Married, in Burlington, New Jersey, Feb. 14, by Rev. Theodore Gould, Miss Rachel J. Romeo, daughter of John H. Romeo, Esq., to Sergeant-Major C. Williams, of Florida.

articles.headline: The Lecture at Concert Hall on Monday Night
articles.summary: On Monday night last Mrs. F. E. W. Harper delivered her lecture before a very large and intelligent audience, at the above named hall. The evening's entertainment was opened by the colored Post band from Camp William Penn, who are remarkably proficient in the musical line.
people: organizer of the winter lecture course (Mr.)

articles.headline: Revivals Going On (Wesley church; Shiloh Baptist)
articles.summary: On last Sabbath evening we preached for Rev. Joseph Smith, of Wesley church, after which those desiring an interest in the prayers of the people of God were invited to the altar, when some eight or nine came forward. Brother Smith not being present, on account of sickness in his family, sent word that he could not be with us on the Sabbath.

articles.headline: The Harrisburg State Convention
articles.summary: Some of our delegates will never forget the kind treatment which they received at the hands of the friends there. We hope that as that city has got her name up through this Convention, the good folks there will continue to maintain it untarnished.

articles.headline: An Appeal for Humanity!
articles.author: Vox Populi
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--My attention has been drawn, recently, to several cases of distress, which, I think, ought to call forth the more tender feelings of our natures; and which, by noticing them in the columns of your valuable journal, may be the means of exciting some action.

articles.headline: Florida Correspondence
articles.author: A. J. Bedford
articles.summary: Fort Pickens, Fla., Nov. 7th, 1864. Mr. Editor:--The change of events, which are so singularly and significantly revolutionising other localities, are not wanting in the place we occupy. ... there is a detachment of four companies, of the gallant 25th, and some other companies, holding this, as a post well garrisoned.

articles.headline: Reflections (22nd U.S.C.T.)
articles.author: W. A. Freeman
articles.summary: It is morning. And as the sun sheds forth his golden rays upon all creation, we can behold in the distance, the glittering bayonets of the true soldiers, the tried veterans of the Twenty-Second U. S. Colored Infantry, that this time one year ago, boasted of its large numbers.

articles.headline: Letter from Florida
articles.author: Enoch K. Miller
articles.summary: Fort Barrancas, Fla., Feb 11th, 1865. Dear Brother Weaver:--We are almost persuaded here that we are detached from the rest of creatures, for the simple reason that our communication with the outer world is severed. But two mails have reached us in two months.

articles.headline: Jubilee of the 22d Regt. U.S.C. Inf. (Soldiers' Literary and Debating Association)
articles.author: W. A. Freeman
articles.summary: Camp 22d Regt. U. S. C. T., Feb 21st, 1865. At the jubilee held on the above date, in the chapel of the 22d Regt. U. S. C. Inf., in honor of the constitutional amendment, and the fall of Charleston, under the supervision of the Soldier's Literary and Debating Association of the 22d Regt.; the following was the programme for the evening.
people: Q. M. Sergt., chairman; president of the Association

articles.headline: From a Drummer Boy (32d Regt. U.S.C.T.)
articles.summary: Fort Edisto Island, S. C., Feb. 17th, 1865. Mr. Editor:--Will you allow me a small space in the columns of your valuable paper, the Christian Recorder. ... It does seem strange to me and my companions in the brave 32d Regt. U. S. C. T., they composing the lion's share of Philadelphians or Pennsylvanians, that all the ladies, especially those who shed tears ... on board of the Continental, when she left our native city ... must have forgotten us.

articles.headline: The Freedmen (letter to the Ladies of the Sanitary of St. Thomas' Church)
articles.summary: We publish the following letter by request of the ladies of the Sanitary of St. Thomas' Church. Alexandria, Feb. 13th, 1865. To the Ladies of the Sanitary of St. Thomas' Church. Accept our hearty thanks for Sanitaries received on the 30th January for sick and wounded soldiers. It is with great pleasure that we acknowledge their receipt; yours being the first colored society which has made us a donation of the kind.

articles.headline: Donation (Bethel A.M.E. Church, Rocky Hill, N.J.)
articles.author: H. Davis
articles.summary: A donation visit was made by the members and well-wishers of the A. M. E. Bethel Church, of Rocky Hill, N. J., for the benefit of the pastor of said church, at which time was collected and given to the steward, to pay over to the pastor, in behalf of said church, the sum of $13.55.

articles.headline: Donation (Mount Pisgah A.M.E. Church, Princeton, N.J.)
articles.author: H. Davis
articles.summary: A donation visit was made by the members and well-wishers of the A. M. E. Mount Pisgah Church, of Princeton, N. J., for the benefit of the pastor of said church. The members of the Female Itinerant Society of said church, proposed and appointed a committee out of their number who prepared a refreshment table at the same time for the same purpose.

articles.headline: Notice (R. W. District Grand Lodge No. 2, Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria)
articles.author: R. H. Gleaves
articles.summary: The officers, representatives, and members of District Grand Lodge, No. 2, Independent order of Good Samaritans, and Daughters of Samaria, of the States of Pennsylvania and Delaware, are hereby notified to attend the Quarterly Meeting of the R. W. D. Grand Lodge, to be held at the new Masonic Hall, South Eleventh street, on Tuesday, March 7th, at 10 o'clock, A. M.

articles.headline: An Appeal (Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia)
articles.summary: The Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia intend giving another fair for the sick and wounded colored soldiers. Feeling that the wants of the soldiers should be attended to by those for whom they are suffering every privation, and doing deeds of valor, we once again earnestly call on the public for assistance.
people: committee, N. E. cor. 11th and Race

articles.headline: Obituary (Martin V. B. Cline)
articles.author: H. W. S.
articles.summary: Died, on the 21st of January, of Small Pox, in the city of New York, Martin V. B. Cline. He was an active member of the A. M. E. Bethel Church of this city, and also a member of Jonathan Fisher's Class. In the death of Martin Cline, the Church has lost a useful member, the family a bright ornament and devoted nephew and cousin.
people: deceased (d. Jan. 21, 1865, New York, smallpox, in his 25th year); member of Bethel

articles.headline: J. Mercer Langston, Esq. (lecture before the Social, Civil and Statistical Association)
articles.summary: This gentleman delivered the fifth lecture of the course before the Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania, on last Thursday evening, at Concert Hall, and was greeted by an appreciative audience. His subject was, 'The War our Emancipator.'

articles.headline: Letter from the Front (Fifth and Sixth Street Passenger Railway)
articles.author: Henry Carpenter Hoyle
articles.summary: Camp near Richmond, Va., February 18th, 1865. Dear Editor:--In looking over the columns of the 'Philadelphia Inquirer,' a few days ago, my eyes fell upon an advertisement, which gave a great deal of pleasure to myself and those of my companions who were at that time with me. It is the success which the people of this country are fast gaining over the once too popular prejudice against our race. The advertisement alluded to, is from the Fifth and Sixth Street Passenger Railway Company, announcing their intention of allowing colored people to ride in the cars of their line.
people: private, Co. F, 43d Regt. U.S.C.T., 25th Corps (letter writer)

articles.headline: From the 43d U.S.C.T.
articles.author: John C. Brock
articles.summary: Camp near Richmond, Va., March 2, 1865. Dear Recorder:--Having been a long time since I have written to you, I now seize the present opportunity to inform your readers where we are, and what we are doing. We are now above the James river, about five miles from Richmond.
people: orderly sergeant, Co. C, 43d U.S.C.T.; preacher (Rev.)

articles.headline: Hon. Wm. D. Kelley (sixth lecture announced)
articles.summary: The sixth and last lecture of the course before the Social, Civil and Statistical Association will be delivered by Hon. Wm. D. Kelley, on next Wednesday evening, 22d inst. The bare mention of the name of Judge Kelley should be sufficient to draw a crowded house.

articles.headline: Revivals (Shiloh Baptist; Bethel; Union Baptist)
articles.summary: For several weeks a protracted meeting has been held in Shiloh Baptist church. The revival there was the most fruitful known for years. Through the instrumentality of the Almighty, about fifty persons, mostly young, have professed a change of heart. On last Sabbath morning about twenty of this number were baptized by Rev. T. D. Miller. ... A protracted meeting, we hear, has commenced at Bethel A. M. E. Church, and one at Union Baptist church, Minster street, opened on last Sabbath evening.

articles.headline: A Noble Representative (Elder Harris of Nashville)
articles.summary: The good people of Nashville, Tenn., are truly proud of Mr. Ransom Harris, who so ably represented them in the late National Convention of Colored Men, held at Syracuse, New York. ... During his stay in our city, Elder Harris accepted an invitation to preach in the Seventh St. Presbyterian Church.

articles.headline: An Acknowledgment (to the Sabbath School Association of Bethel Church)
articles.author: S. L. Daffin
articles.summary: To the Committee of the Sabbath School Association of Bethel Church, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Dear Friends:--The box sent by you, containing clothing, books, papers, &c., reached here quite opportunely. Please accept my sincere thanks on behalf of the freed people of this city, for your very liberal contribution. Norfolk, Va., 21st 2d mo., '65.

articles.headline: Notice (Wilberforce collection, Mount Pisgah A.M.E. Church, Princeton, N.J.)
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--Will you favor me with a place in our beloved 'Recorder' for this notice. The contribution was taken up on the 5th of March, 1865, in the A. M. E. Mount Pisgah Church, in Princeton, N. J., for the purpose of assisting in making the last payment for the Wilberforce University.

articles.headline: A Christian Visiting Trip
articles.author: Thos. S. Parrent
articles.summary: Philada., Pa., March 9th, 1865. On December 31st, 1864, in company with Rev. N. A. Turpin, elder of Hollidaysburg circuit, I left Williamsport for Bellefontaine. ... I then came to the city on February 2d, and found Rev. Jos. H. Smith holding a protracted meeting. I spent several nights with him, and many were brought into the fold of Christ.

articles.headline: Thanks!! (preachers' meeting at Bethel for a superannuated father)
articles.author: T. Gould
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--Allow me the favor, through the columns of your paper, to say to the brethren who met in the preachers' meeting in Bethel Church, on the 31st ult., that the small donation of $6.50, which they contributed to the Rev. [?] Holcomb, I delivered to him, with their kindest regards, for one of the fathers who has been worn out in the service of the church.

articles.headline: Notice (Reading Circuit Quarterly Meetings)
articles.author: John Henson
articles.summary: Reading Circuit Quarterly Meetings. Reading, Penna., first Saturday and Sunday in April, Quarterly Conference; Second Saturday in April, Quarterly Meetings, Great Valley, Pa., third Saturday and Sunday; Downingtown, 4th do do; Birdsboro, 5th do do; Hollow Valley, Centreville, 1st do do in May.

articles.headline: A Mean Thief (W. R. Decordover robbed)
articles.summary: We learn from Mr. W. R. Decordover, of No. 419 south Seventh street, that one day last week some unprincipled person, whom he left in his store during his absence, took the occasion to purloin some $25 [VERIFY] from his trunk. Part of the money was in silver.
people: proprietor, periodical depot, 419 South Seventh street (Mr.)

articles.headline: Reading in Concert Hall (S. Morgan Smith)
articles.summary: On last Friday evening, Mr. S. Morgan Smith gave his first reading in the above named Hall. His programme consisted of selections from Shakespeare, Whittier, and some others of our best poets. A lack of space forbids any extended criticism at present; but we may, at a future date, compare the merits of our two pioneer readers, Mr. J. Henry Smith and Mr. S. Morgan Smith.

articles.headline: Lecture (Hon. William D. Kelley, Social, Civil and Statistical Association)
articles.author: William Still
articles.summary: Hon. William D. Kelley will deliver the 6th Lecture of the course before the Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania, on Wednesday evening, March 22, in Concert Hall. Subject: 'The War, and the Rights of Humanity.' Miss E. T. Greenfield, the celebrated 'Black Swan,' will sing on the occasion.

articles.headline: Aid for the Sufferers at Charleston, S.C.
articles.summary: Philadelphia, February 26th, 1865. At a meeting of the former residents of Charleston, S. C., held in this city on the 2[?] of February, Mr. Charles L. Ferrette was called to the Chair, and R. M. Adger appointed Secretary. The President stated the object of the meeting: to devise ways and means by which we can send aid to our suffering people in the city of Charleston, who stand in need of our immediate relief.
people: depot, at Wm. Still's, Fifth & Arch streets

articles.headline: Notice (last quarterly meeting, Bethel A.M.E., Wilmington, Del.)
articles.author: H. J. Rhodes
articles.summary: The last quarterly meeting for this Conference year of the A. M. E. Bethel Church, in the city of Wilmington, Delaware, will be held on the first Sunday in April, the 1st [sic], 1865, no preventing Providence, at which time we expect to have several ministers to assist us, the Lord willing.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meetings (Princeton, Brunswick, Rocky Hill, Sourland Mountain)
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: Quarterly Meeting in Princeton, on the 9th of April. Quarterly Meeting in Brunswick, on the 16th of April. Quarterly Meeting at Rocky Hill. Quarterly Meeting at Sowerlin [Sourland] Mountain. Rev. Henry Davis, Elder. Rev. Wm. Otter [VERIFY], Deacon.

articles.headline: Notice (Burlington Circuit Quarterly Meetings)
articles.author: T. Gould
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meetings of the Burlington Circuit will be held as follows: Mount Holly, April 1st and 2d. Burlington, April 8th and 9th. Evesham, April 22 and 23d. T. Gould, Minister.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: On the 9th of March, by Rev. J. C. Gibbs, Sergeant J. Wesley Simpson, 24th [?] U.S.C.T., of this city, to Miss Mary S. Jackson, of Boston, Massachusetts. (Boston papers, please copy.) On February 9th, 1865, by the Rev. Jos. R. M[...], Mr. William Sparrow, of Newbern, North Carolina, to Miss Mary E. Mandiff [?], of this city.

articles.headline: Obituary (Eliza Ann Davis)
articles.author: T. Gould
articles.summary: Sister Eliza Ann Davis, daughter of Robert and Ann Davis, departed this life, in full triumph of a blessed immortality, on the 21st day of January, 1865, aged 23 years, 9 months, and 27 days. She embraced religion about six years ago. Burlington, N. J., March 13 [?], 1865.

articles.headline: Shrouding and Laying Out of the Dead (Mrs. Highgates)
articles.summary: Shrouding and Laying Out of the Dead. Mrs. Highgates most earnestly solicits the patronage and attention of the generous public and her friends, as she is now in the business of shrouding and laying out of the dead. No. 1026 Barley street, bet. 10th & 11th, & Lombard & Pine Sts.

articles.headline: Action! Action! Action!
articles.author: Stanford
articles.summary: ... Let us contend lawfully, rightfully and perseveringly for our political rights, in common with other men. ... As a gentleman, in our presence, this morning, (Monday, 20th,) remarked, 'Sir, do not push the question of your people voting. It is not ripe yet. Public opinion is against you.' ... No shouting yet! Go on and complete the victory!

articles.headline: Bethel Sabbath-School Concert
articles.summary: The Sabbath-School connected with the Bethel A. M. E. Church intend giving a grand concert in Sansom Street Hall, on Thursday evening, April 6th, 1865. There have been engaged several well-known artists. ... A few [tickets] are for sale at our office, 619 Pine street. Price 25 cents.

articles.headline: Judge Kelley's Lecture
articles.summary: On Wednesday evening Hon. W. D. Kelley delivered the sixth and final lecture of this Winter's course, before the Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania. The Hall was crowded with a most appreciative audience. Miss E. T. Greenfield, Miss Kate Laurier, Mr. W. Sturges, and Count J. De Cliff, sang, and the Post Band from Camp Wm. Penn, enlivened the occasion with some very good music. Mr. R. Purves introduced the lecturer.

articles.headline: Notice (Mrs. Lucy Ann Nelson sought by her sister)
articles.summary: If Mrs. Lucy Ann Nelson, who was a member of Bethel A. M. E. Church before the split, will call at our office, she will hear of her sister, Mary E. Griffin.
people: former member of Bethel A.M.E. Church 'before the split' (Mrs.)

articles.headline: The Drama of Outrages
articles.author: Britton Lanier
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--It was with feelings of the deepest indignation that I perused the columns of the Press to-day. From said perusal I see that no less than two most fiendish and brutal acts were perpetrated in less than twenty-four hours. Two soldiers, wearing the United States uniform ... were ruthlessly forced from the front platform of one of the street cars of this city, so long honored and pointed to as the City of Brotherly Love!
people: clergyman attacked while aiding the beaten man (Rev.)

articles.headline: A Statement Corrected (Burlington, N.J.)
articles.summary: To the Editor of the Christian Recorder:--In your issue of February 25th, we find a notice, stating that the rites of matrimony had been performed between two couples, by Rev. Theo. Gould, in Burlington, N.J., on February 14th. We would here say that the report is without the least foundation.

articles.headline: From the 41st U.S.C.T.
articles.author: Wm. H. Fray
articles.summary: Army of the James, Camp Forty-first U. S. C. T., March 9, '65. Mr. Editor:--I have come to the conclusion to try my hand, for the first time, in penning a few lines for your columns respecting the 41st U. S. C. T. Infantry. We left Camp William Penn on the 13th of October. ... marched down Second street to Prime, and down Prime to the Refreshment Saloon.

articles.headline: Notice (Union League Association officers)
articles.summary: At the regular meeting of the Union League Association, held on Thursday evening, March 17th, at the Hall, the following persons were elected officers. (Also named, reading uncertain: Jesse E. Glasgow [VERIFY] (vice-president (middle initial E or K)); Joseph W. Cassey [VERIFY] (secretary (printed Cussey/Cassey)).)

articles.headline: Notice (Westchester Circuit quarterly meeting)
articles.author: Ed. Laws
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meeting on this circuit will be held at Westchester, Pa., on the first Saturday and Sunday in April. Rev. Ed. Laws, Pastor. Rev. Elisha Weaver, Presiding Elder.

articles.headline: Notice (Horntown Circuit quarterly conference)
articles.author: Jno. C. Cornish
articles.summary: The Quarterly Conference of Horntown circuit will be held at Horntown, on the second Saturday and Sabbath in April, commencing at 3 o'clock, P. M. Rev. Jno. C. Cornish, Pastor. Rev. E. Weaver, Elder in charge.

events.name: Watch-night service at Bethel Church
events.description: The editor attended the watch-meeting at Bethel on Saturday night, Dec. 31, 1864. Sunday Jan. 1 was communion Sabbath at Bethel. That night, by arrangement with Brother Stanford (A. L. Stanford), the editor spoke for the Recorder at the A. M. E. Union Church: collection $26.05, some sixty papers sold and two annual subscribers; few members present, congregation more than three-fourths white. Stanford has prevailed on the superintendent of the Union Sabbath School to give an exhibition for the paper.

events.name: Holiday fairs of the Philadelphia churches
events.location: Masonic Hall; Concert Hall; Hurst Street Church; Wesley Church, Lombard St.; Union A. M. E. Church
events.description: City Notices: the ladies of Bethel Church held a fair in Masonic Hall for the colored sick and wounded soldiers, crowded every night; Monday and Tuesday proceeds went to Wilberforce University. St. Thomas' Church held a fair for the sick and wounded soldiers in Concert Hall, then removed it to their own lecture-room. Sisters of the A. M. E. Hurst Street Church, of Wesley Church (Lombard St., in the basement) and of the A. M. E. Union Church also held holiday fairs.

events.name: Organ presentation at Zion Wesley Church
events.description: Rev. J. P. Trusty, pastor of Zion Wesley Church, invited the editor. A sister of the church donated an organ; Rev. J. C. Gibbs presented it to Brother Trusty on the donor's behalf, who gave it to the Trustees. Sergeant-Major Green then gave an eloquent speech. A Ladies' Festival for the pastor's benefit was held downstairs.

events.name: Lecture by Mrs. F. E. W. Harper at Bethel, 'The Mission of the War'
events.description: Frances E. W. Harper lectured at Bethel on 'The Mission of the War'. The editor ranks her above Miss Anna Dickerson; a pretty good house but not as large as hoped.

events.name: Debt jubilee at the (Central) Presbyterian Church, Rev. Mr. Reeve, pastor
events.location: Presbyterian Church (Rev. Mr. Reeve, pastor), Philadelphia
events.description: Jubilee on paying off the last debt on the church, Wednesday 28th ultimo. Rev. Dr. Brainerd spoke (the editor missed him); the Hon. Mr. Pierce praised the Presbyterian Church and congregation; the choir was drawn from other churches; refreshments in the lecture-room. Mr. Jones thanked the donors on behalf of the church, who had bought four silver cups for the best collectors; Mr. Glasco was second-best in raising contributions; a gentleman had offered $1,000 if the balance were raised. Rev. Mr. Reeve is J. B. Reeve of Central Presbyterian (identification, not printed here).

events.name: Anniversary of the Banneker Institute
events.location: National Hall, Market street above Twelfth, Philadelphia
events.description: Monday night, Jan. 2, 1865. Hall completely crowded. Mr. J. C. White, Jr., chairman, called the meeting to order; Rev. Jeremiah Turpin of Allegheny prayed; Mr. Taylor read letters received; Mr. O. C. Catto (printed so; one of the teachers of the High School, i.e. O. V. Catto of the ICY) gave an address; the colored Band from Camp William Penn played; Professor Bassett read letters from Frederick Douglass and Charles Sumner explaining their absence; Rev. H. H. Garnet of Washington, D. C. spoke.
attendees: address; teacher of the High School (printed 'O. C.')

events.name: Concert of the Financial Enterprise Association
events.description: Concert on 'last Tuesday evening' at Sansom Street Hall under the Financial Enterprise Association. Performers: Misses Greenfield and Freeman, Count Cliff, pupils of Miss Greenfield (the 'Swan'), Prof. Koenig (piano, march from Faust), Mr. J. J. Spelman (debut, duet with Miss Freeman). Date computed as Tuesday Jan. 3, 1865.

events.name: Bethel Sabbath School Christmas celebration
events.description: Monday 26th, half-past ten, the school assembled and was addressed by Revs. Moore and Smith, B. Y. Dingle, Esq., formerly an officer of the institution, and Mr. L. R. Seymour, the present superintendent; scholars regaled; teachers' social re-union.
attendees: speaker; former officer of the school (Esq.)

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League ovation to Rev. Calvin Fairbank
events.location: National Hall, Market street above Twelfth, Philadelphia
events.description: Grand public ovation to Rev. Calvin Fairbank, sentenced in Kentucky to 150 lashes and fifteen years' imprisonment for aiding fugitives; he will give an account of nearly thirteen years of captivity, accompanied by his wife. Tickets 25 cents; doors at 7, exercises at 8. Committee of Arrangement: A. M. Green, Dr. Jas. M. C. Crummel, Jos. C. Bustill, J. C. White, Jr., Chas. B. Colly, Rev. E. Nearer (sic, probably E. Weaver), David D. Turner, George W. Goins, John W. Simpson, O. V. Catto, John H. Colbert, John W. Page, P. Norman Judah.

events.name: Grand Lodge of Pennsylvania (Prince Hall) installation of officers
events.location: Grand Lodge hall, South Eleventh Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Elected Dec. 5, installed Dec. 27, 1864: Jonathan Davis, R. W. G. Master; Nathaniel L. Durham, Deputy R. W. G. Master; Aaron P. Faucett, R. W. S. G. Warden; Ralph Gilmore, R. W. J. G. Warden; John G. Dutton, R. W. G. Treasurer; Alfred S. Cassey, R. W. G. Secretary. Grand Chaplains: James Frisby, Wm. G. Cooper, Redman Faucett. District Deputy Grand Masters: Chas. H. Cann of Harrisburg (Dauphin, Franklin, Cumberland, Lancaster), Hannibal C. Molson of Lewistown (Mifflin and Centre), Geo. B. Vashon of Pittsburg (Allegheny). Edward Matheist, S. G. Deacon; William Shipley, J. G. Deacon; Henry O'Donnell, S. G. Steward; Joseph C. Green, J. G. Steward; Jonathan C. Miller, G. Marshal; Philip N. Judah, G. Sword Bearer; Moses N. Jones, G. Pursuivant; Perry Mitchell, G. Tyler. Committee on Land Marks: Wm. H. Riley, R. H. Gleaves, Wm. E. Gipson, Hans Shaddand, James Needham. On By-Laws: Wm. E. Gipson, Hans Shaddand, F. R. Belasques, George White, Alfred S. Cassey. On Correspondence: R. H. Gleaves, Redman Faucett, Edward Y. Venning, Thos. H. Davis, Thos. M. Cline. On Finance: P. N. Judah, R. H. Gleaves, Joseph H. Dyer (printed Doyer?), Theodore Young, Charles H. Edwards. On Charity: Wm. E. Gipson, Samuel B. Collins, Thos. D. Jordon, Wm. Cooper, George W. Woolford.
attendees: R. W. Grand Secretary; by-laws committee
Grand Sword Bearer; finance committee (as P. N. Judah)

events.name: Grand Lodge of New Jersey (A. Y. M.) installation at Burlington
events.description: Annual communication of the R. W. G. Lodge of the A. Y. M. for New Jersey, Burlington, Dec. 27, 1864 (Philadelphia Conference territory). Installed: James Dolphin, R. W. G. M.; Freeman Gould, R. W. D. G. M.; Henry Carter, R. W. S. G. W.; Wm. A. Longfellow, R. W. J. G. W.; O. L. Davis, R. W. G. T.; Joshua Woodlin, R. W. G. S. Grand Chaplains Rev. Ebenezer (printed Ehinezar) Man and Benjamin Jackson. District Deputies: Benjamin F. Brown (Middlesex and Essex), John H. Romeo (Burlington and Mercer), Henry H. Williams (Salem), Edward Wright (Cumberland and Cape May), Isaac Wells (Camden and Gloucester). David Taylor, S. G. D.; Charles Faucet, J. G. D.; York Williams, J. G. D.; Robert Williams, J. G. S.; Charles Williams, G. M.; Charles Topeman, G. S.; James A. Hill, G. P.; John Spencer, G. Tyler; John H. Bean, G. Lecturer. Land Marks: H. Mackey, Peter D. Hedges, Chas. Dumont. By-Laws: O. L. Davis, Charles T. Gardner (reading uncertain), J. Woodlin. Charity committee names (Daniel Cuff, Levi ...) partly illegible under an ink blot. Attest J. Woodlin, G. Sec.
attendees: R. W. Grand Secretary (Rev. Joshua Woodlin of the Philadelphia Conference, identification in notes)

events.name: Concert and festival for the A. M. E. Church at Frankford
events.description: Grand concert and festival, Thursday evening Jan. 12, for the benefit of the A. M. E. Church at Frankford; several distinguished speakers; tickets 25 cents; cars leave Sixth and Powell at 5 1/2 and 6 P. M.

events.name: Home for Aged and Infirm Colored People: first annual meeting of contributors
events.location: West room of National Hall, Market St. above 12th, 2d story, Philadelphia
events.description: First annual meeting of contributors, Thursday Jan. 12, 8 o'clock; several speakers. Signed M. Balderston, Secretary (probably the white Quaker secretary; not linked).

events.name: J. Anderson Raymond lecture for the Sabbath School of Scott's Union Baptist Church
events.location: Scott's Union Baptist church, Minster street, Philadelphia
events.description: Lecture 'Africa and her People: their rights and wrongs considered, and their future prosperity'; admittance ten cents; proceeds to the Sabbath School.

events.name: West Chester Aid Society fair and supper for a new church
events.description: The ladies of the Aid Society of West Chester held a fair (committee of seven) and on Dec. 30 a supper, to raise means to build a new church; Rev. John C. Cornish present during the fair. At the supper Harmony Lodge No. 21 of the A. Y. M., with members from Philadelphia, the I. O. of B. and S. of L. and C. (Love and Charity) of M. B. T., No. 3, West Chester, with members from Philadelphia, and the Odd Fellows appeared in regalia. Rev. Stephen Smith spoke on Love and Charity and the admission of ladies to secret societies. The sisters raised seventy dollars. Letter signed E. A. C., dated Jan. 6, 1865.

events.name: Quarterly meeting at Media, Pa.
events.location: A. M. E. church, Media, Pa.
events.description: Quarterly meeting held Saturday and Sabbath (Jan. 7-8, 1865) by Rev. E. Laws, with a love-feast at night. The church building belongs to 'our people' and is said to be the first built in Media; the editor urges a better one. One more quarterly meeting remains on Brother Laws's circuit this Conference year.

events.name: Recorder subscription drive results to January 10, 1865
events.description: Agents' returns: Rev. J. M. Alexander, Helena, 12 cash; Rev. W. J. Davis, Galesburg, 3; Rev. H. R. Revels, 4 cash 7 unpaid; Rev. E. B. Davis, 1 cash 2 unpaid; Rev. S. Watts, 1 cash 4 unpaid; Rev. W. H. Norris, Norristown, 7 cash; Miss Mary Still, 13 cash 1 unpaid; Rev. Thomas Cooper, 4 cash 2 unpaid; Rev. Ed. Laws, 1 cash 5 unpaid; Rev. J. W. Malone, 5 cash; Rev. C. Burch, 12 cash; Rev. W. Davidson, 1; G. W. Terley, Esq., Virginia City, Idaho Territory, 5; Rev. E. T. Williams, 15; Rev. J. Hamilton, 2; Rev. William Jackson, 2; Rev. W. T. Ralph, 1 unpaid; Rev. H. J. Johnson, 1; Rev. A. T. Wood, 3; Rev. W. A. Dove (New Orleans), 22; Rev. J. A. Jay, 1 unpaid; Rev. W. Arbuckle, 4; Chaplain G. H. White, 28th U. S. C. T. (printed 20th in the list), 18; Rev. E. D. Davis, Xenia, 4 cash 3 unpaid; Rev. John M. Brown, 1; Chaplain H. M. Turner (1st U. S. C. T.), 55 cash; Rev. L. Patterson, 2; Rev. T. G. Stuart, 4 cash 11 unpaid; Rev. J. Lynch, 1; Q. M. Serg't Payne, 27th U. S. C. T., 5; Rev. A. Till, 2; Rev. Theo. Gould, 1; Mrs. Cropper, 1; Mr. James Brown, 2; Rev. S. T. Jones, 3 cash 3 unpaid; Rev. F. Myers, 1; Rev. L. W. Bass, 2; Rev. W. M. Johnson, 1; J. W. Wilkerson, 6; Rev. R. Bridges, 3; Rev. W. W. Grimes, 1; Chaplain E. K. Miller, 25th U. S. C. T., 130 unpaid. Only Philadelphia-area agents are linked.

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association lecture: Rev. J. Sella Martin, 'The friends of the Union in England'
events.description: Second lecture of the SCSA course, Wednesday Jan. 25; Miss E. T. Greenfield, the 'Black Swan', volunteered to sing. Tickets at the Recorder office (619 Pine), Lebanon Cemetery office, the Philadelphia Institute, or the committee: Isaiah C. Wears, U. B. Vidal, J. C. Gibbs, J. C. White, Sr., Wm. P. Price, S. Morgan Smith, Redman Faucet, Chas. H. Bustill, Morris Hall, Stephen Smith; Wm. Still, chairman of the committee of arrangements. Doors 6 1/2, exercises at 8. (The course's proceeds were pledged in part to the streetcar rights campaign, see Jan 7.)

events.name: Funeral discourse for Emeline Jackson at Wesley A. M. E. Church
events.location: A. M. E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Revs. H. Davis and J. H. Smith preached from the 23d Psalm on the death of Sister Emeline Jackson: born in Delaware in 1814 (as printed; the stated age 'about 50' fits), brought to Philadelphia as a child by her mother, married at 14, converted at 20 and joined Zion A. M. E. Church, Lombard Street, later Wesley A. M. E., Hurst Street; ill four years; died Dec. 26 (1864). Signed Rev. Henry Davis.

events.name: Philadelphia mass meeting at Franklin Hall to organize delegate elections for the State Equal Rights Convention
events.description: 'Last evening' (the issue is dated Saturday Jan. 28, so probably Friday Jan. 27, 1865), at the call of the Executive Board of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League. Dr. James M'Crummill elected president, with a large number of vice presidents and secretaries (not named). John C. Bustill offered resolutions, unanimously adopted: Philadelphia divided into six representative districts, each with a committee of thirteen appointed by the Chair to call public meetings to elect delegates to the Harrisburg convention of Feb. 8: 1st, Frankford; 2d, West Philadelphia; 3d, north of Callowhill street; 4th, river to river from Callowhill to Spruce; 5th, west from Tenth and south of Spruce; 6th, east from Tenth and south of Spruce. The committees are to form auxiliary Leagues and enlist churches, lodges and other organizations. District meetings to be held during the coming week.

events.name: Streetcar rights: Recorder endorses Senator Lowry's speech in the Pennsylvania Senate
events.description: STREETCAR topic. The editor prints (on pages not in our copy) the speech of Hon. Morrow B. Lowry delivered in the Pennsylvania Senate on Jan. 10, 1865, and comments: 'The question of allowing the colored people of Philadelphia to ride in the city passenger railway cars, is one that has been considerably agitated of late'; Equal Rights on one side, 'that arch fiend and monster, Prejudice' on the other; colored taxpayers pay the same taxes. 'We advise the Legislature to take the advice of Mr. Lowry.'

events.name: Christian Commission third anniversary, Academy of Music: 13th Amendment news announced
events.description: Third anniversary of the U.S. Christian Commission at the Academy of Music on the 31st ult. George H. Stuart, President of the Commission, announced a telegraphic despatch from Speaker S. Colfax that the constitutional amendment had passed the House, 119 to 56; the news was received with loud and long-continued applause. Prayer by Rev. C. P. Krauth, D.D.; Rev. Dr. Bomberger read the Psalm; report by Mr. C. Dinord [as printed] of Boston; address by Rev. Alexander Reed. (White-run event; recorded for the 13th Amendment topic. No Black participants named.)

events.name: Revivals in the Philadelphia churches ('The Good Lord at Work')
events.description: Mission A.M.E. Church: Rev. W. W. Winder has had his prayers answered; many souls awakened. Wesley Zion A.M.E. Church (the Zion A.M.E. Church, Wesley), Rev. J. B. Trusty pastor: two or three weeks of revival; on Sunday night the 29th the editor preached there to a large congregation; Brother Haukerstern [VERIFY], a deacon, announced that on account of the pastor's illness (Brother Trusty) the protracted effort would be brought to a close. A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street, Rev. Joseph Smith pastor (Elder Smith): crowds of sinners at the altar nightly; meetings continuing. Burlington, N.J.: Rev. Theodore Gould, the pastor, has been conducting a revival for a week or two.
attendees: pastor (Rev.), Wesley Zion A.M.E. Church; ill
pastor (Rev.; 'Elder Smith'), A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst St.

events.name: Love Feast at Bethel Church
events.description: A Love Feast was held at Bethel Church on last Monday night, the 30th ult.; 'one of the best that we have had the pleasure of attending for some time. There were quite a number of our white friends present.' No names.

events.name: Mr. John H. Smith's Reading, Sansom Street Hall
events.description: Mr. John H. Smith gave his first public Reading, selections from American and English authors, to a large audience. Smith was a member of the class that received the diploma of the Institute for Colored Youth in 1862; his first public notice came when he recited Boker's 'Black Regiment' at the organization of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League last December. He recited from Antony's oration, Cavalry Sheridan, T. Buchanan Read's 'Sheridan's Ride' and Poe's Raven. Miss Caroline R. Le Count, also a graduate of the Institute for Colored Youth, assisted, reading Longfellow's 'Launch of the Ship', Mrs. F. D. Hemans's 'Bernardo Del Carpio', Whittier's 'Prisoner for Debt' and Mrs. Norton's 'Bingen on the Rhine'. Mr. William H. Maurice, 'a gentleman of cultivated taste, and high social standing', introduced Smith, saying that four years ago he would have shrunk in horror if asked to introduce a Colored Man. Miss Rachel A. Freeman and Mr. I. D. Cliff [VERIFY] sang. The writer compares Le Count and Smith with Madam Ruffin and Mr. Richardson; another Reading is contemplated.

events.name: Ordination of deacons, Union Baptist Church
events.description: On Lord's day, the 22d ult., five deacons were ordained. Scriptures read by Rev. Elisha Weaver; prayer by Rev. Charles Rodgers; ordination sermon by Rev. T. D. Miller from Acts 6:3-4; prayer by Rev. Caleb Burns; the minister in charge, Rev. Jas. Hamilton, assisted by Revs. Rodgers and Leonard, laid on hands; the charge given by Rev. Chauncy A. Leonard. Declared regularly ordained Deacons: John Erwin [VERIFY], John Boling, Reuben Coote, Malachi Ferrell [VERIFY], and Wm. Thompson.
attendees: minister in charge (Rev.), Union Baptist Church

events.name: Wilberforce Bazaar at the Institute (ladies of Bethel Church)
events.description: The ladies of Bethel Church have been holding a Fair since Monday evening for the benefit of Wilberforce University, in the handsomely decorated old Institute, to help the Trustees meet the last payment on the University, $5,000, due by the 10th of March. Expected to close Saturday evening. No individuals named.

events.name: Lecture on Phrenology by Prof. J. A. Raymond, Union Baptist Church
events.location: Union Baptist Church, Minster St., Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: Prof. J. A. Raymond, who has contributed several articles on phrenology to the Recorder, will lecture on Phrenology in Union Baptist Church, Minster St., Thursday evening next, 9th inst. Admission 10 cents; tickets at the Recorder office.
attendees: lecturer (Prof.); also printed J. Anderson Raymond

events.name: Musical banquet at Philadelphia Institute for Rev. W. H. Winder
events.description: A grand musical banquet will be given at Philadelphia Institute on Tuesday evening next [Feb. 7], in aid of Rev. W. H. Winder, pastor of Zion Mission Church. Admission 15 cents.

events.name: St. Thomas' Colored Episcopal Church ladies' sanitary committee: fair at Concert Hall, thanks
events.description: 'Thanks! Thanks!!' The ladies' sanitary committee of St. Thomas' Colored Episcopal Church, auxiliary to the United States Sanitary Commission, thank all who supported the fair recently held by them in Concert Hall; despite unfavorable weather and heavy expenditures it realized $1,226.75. Signed Mrs. T. J. Bowers, Pres.; Lucy Henson, Sec. Philadelphia, Feb. 3d, 1865. Editorial note: the association is under the special control of ladies well known for Christian sympathy; it has sent several boxes of goods to sufferers from Gen. Sherman's portion of the army, with another box nearly ready; net proceeds over $1,200.
attendees: president, St. Thomas' ladies' sanitary committee

events.name: Fair at the Institute for Rev. W. H. Winder (Zion Mission Church): committee thanked
events.description: Rev. W. H. Winder thanks the committee who, despite a violent rainstorm that flooded the streets, held an entertainment at the Institute for his benefit and presented him, clear of all expenses, with $12.30 [as printed]. Committee: Mrs. E. Dade, Mrs. A. Cregg, Mrs. A. Johnson, Mrs. Lock, Mrs. E. Ates [VERIFY], Miss J. Jones, Mr. William Young, Mr. B. Syers, Mr. J. Pitterman. Signed W. H. W. Winder [as printed], Philadelphia. (Probably the Feb 7 'musical banquet' announced Feb 4.)

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights Convention, Harrisburg (editor's report)
events.description: Weaver's report, dated Harrisburg Feb. 8 and 9. He arrived Feb. 7 in a heavy snowstorm with a number of the Philadelphia Delegation, met by Mr. Hughes; introduced by 'our worthy friend, Mr. Adger, of Philadelphia' to Miss Ellen Spence, who lodged him with her parents Mr. and Mrs. Spence. Feb. 8, 10 a.m., A.M.E. Zion church: called to order by William Nesbit of Altoona; O. V. Catto of Philadelphia secretary; prayer by Rev. John Price, local preacher of Harrisburg. Speeches by David Bowser (on motion of Elisha Weaver), Mr. Williams of Hollidaysburg, John Allen of Philadelphia, J. J. Wright of Wilkesbarre, Aaron Still of Reading, Elisha Weaver. Officers: President Rev. John Peck, Pittsburg; Vice-Presidents Rev. Elisha Weaver (Philadelphia), Moses Brown (Hollidaysburg), O. L. C. Hughes (Harrisburg), James Davenger (Pittston), John Welsh (Bellefont), William Nesbit (Altoona); Secretaries O. V. Catto (Philadelphia), A. T. Harris (Hampton), Rev. Redmond Faucett (Philadelphia); Business Committee Prof. George B. Vashon (Allegheny), Daniel Williams, D. B. Bowser, Sergeant A. M. Green, B. G. Palpruss [as printed], James Henry, Mr. Nelson of Harrisburg. Members paid two dollars each. Evening of Feb. 8 addresses by Sergeant-Major Green, Hon. Mr. Lowry of the Senate, John Allen and Prof. Vashon. Feb. 9: Weaver presided; prayer by Rev. W. Alston; declaration of rights adopted; afternoon resolution by Mr. Wright on colored schools (colored teachers for colored schools; a school wherever twenty scholars). Feb. 10: financial report adopted after objections; resolution regretting W. L. Garrison's course at the Massachusetts Anti-Slavery Society carried almost unanimously; resolution commending the Christian Recorder carried unanimously; adjourned sine die at 5. Evening: house filled with white and colored, members of the Legislature present; addresses by Rev. Wm. J. Alston (emigration to the South), J. J. Wright, O. V. Catto ('a teacher in the High School in Philada.') and Elisha Weaver; Financial Committee chairman Mr. Gordon of Philadelphia took a collection; collation by the ladies of Harrisburg (Miss Mary Williams prominent). Delegates left between 2 and 3 a.m.
attendees: secretary; speaker; teacher, ICY high school
opening prayer (Rev. W. Alston); evening speaker on emigration to the South

events.name: Celebration in memory of Bishop Richard Allen, Bethel Church
events.description: On Tuesday night the 14th instant at Bethel. Bishop Wayman spoke (Rome her Caesar, Germany her Luther, England her Wesley, America her Washington, Jefferson and Lincoln; our people should never forget Richard Allen); he noted that a few days earlier, on this very spot, the mother church after forty years sent delegates who acknowledged the A.M.E. Church as equals. Rev. Stephen Smith spoke: he had known Allen many years; Allen belonged to one Mr. Chew; he told of the gallery ejection at St. George's. Elisha Weaver spoke briefly. Elder Moore (Bethel's pastor) promised more remarks another time and gave out a long-metre hymn. Audience small because of inclement weather.

events.name: Weaver to preach at Bethel and Wesley churches
events.location: Bethel Church and Wesley Church, Philadelphia
events.description: The editor will preach to-morrow at 3 o'clock in Bethel Church for Rev. Mr. Moore ('The New Birth; or, Being Born Again'), and at night for Rev. J. B. Trusty at Wesley Church ('Justification by Faith, and Peace with God').

events.name: Frederick Douglass lecture 'Equality before the Law', Concert Hall; silver service presented by ladies of St. Thomas'
events.description: Third lecture of the course before the Social, Civil, and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania. At 8 o'clock Douglass came on the platform with the president of the Association, Mr. Isaiah Ware [as printed], and ladies and gentlemen 'among whom was no distinction in regard to color or caste'. He spoke nearly two hours on 'Equality before the law' to thousands of white and colored listeners; hall and aisles crowded. Afterward the ladies of St. Thomas' P.E. Church, through Mr. Vidal, presented Douglass a silver service (salver, pitcher and pair of goblets) bought by voluntary contributions from colored citizens, collected by a committee of ladies of that church. Mr. Love, a white gentleman, offered a resolution, unanimously adopted, opposing any complexional distinction in the elective franchise. Miss E. T. Greenfield, 'the Black Swan, of our city', sang; afterward a trio, 'Believe Me' by Verdi, by Miss Greenfield, Miss Kate Lanier and Mr. Cliff.
attendees: president, Social, Civil and Statistical Association (printed 'Ware')

events.name: Concert and Exhibition at Union A.M.E. Church: pupils of Prof. A. Burris
events.description: Concert and exhibition at Union A.M.E. Church in aid of the Christian Recorder and Wilberforce University on Thursday evening, March 2d, by the pupils of Prof. A. Burris, 'so well known as a successful teacher of music'. Tickets 25 cents at the Recorder counter, 619 Pine street.

events.name: Colored People's Union League Association: grand demonstration for the 13th Amendment (announced)
events.description: The Colored People's Union League Association will give a grand demonstration at Concert Hall, Chestnut Street, in honor of the amendment to the Constitution abolishing slavery, on Friday evening, March 3d. Addresses by Jno. S. Rock, Esq. (Boston), Revs. P. Brooks, A. L. Stanford, Wm. J. Alston, T. D. Miller, and Messrs. Love and Nicholson. Music by a band and a chorus of upwards of one hundred children under the direction of William A. Burris. A presentation during the evening. Tickets 25 cents. J. C. Bowers, President; G. W. Goines, St. George Taylor, Secretaries. Editorial note urges all similar organizations, Masonic orders and societies to attend.
attendees: president, Colored People's Union League Association

events.name: Mrs. F. E. W. Harper lectures at Concert Hall
events.description: Lecture 'The Cause and Effects of the War, or, in other words, the mission of the war' by Mrs. F. E. W. Harper, before one of the largest audiences of 'this winter's course, by Mr. Wm. Still.' Music by the colored Post band from Camp William Penn; Miss Greenfield, 'the celebrated Black Swan,' accompanied a young lady at the piano and sang. She spoke nearly an hour and a half; the band closed with 'We'll rally round the flag, boys.' Date computed: 'Monday night last' before Saturday, March 4.

events.name: 22nd U.S.C.T. jubilee for the 13th Amendment and the fall of Charleston
events.location: chapel of the 22d Regt. U.S.C. Infantry, in the field (Virginia)
events.description: Under the Soldier's Literary and Debating Association of the 22d Regt. (a Camp William Penn regiment). Programme: chairman Q. M. Sergt. Wm. H. Warner called the house to order; prayer by Rev. Christopher C. Burroughs, chaplain; address by Rev. C. C. Burroughs on the constitutional amendment; 'Hail, Columbia' by the regimental brass band; address by Hon. Thomas Morris Chester, of the Press, on the amendment and the fall of Charleston; 'America'; vote of thanks to the speakers on motion of Hospital Steward Clement B. Baker; vote of thanks to Lt. Col. J. C. Terry, commanding, on motion of W. A. Freeman; Terry's reply; three cheers on motion of Sergt. Major Wm. L. Miller; 'Star-Spangled Banner'; adjourned with benediction by Q. M. Sergeant Wm. H. Warner, president of the Association. W. A. Freeman, Secretary.
attendees: Q. M. Sergt., chairman and president of the Association

events.name: St. Thomas' Church Ladies' Sanitary sends supplies to Alexandria hospitals
events.location: St. Thomas' Church, Philadelphia (donors); L'Ouverture general hospital, Alexandria, Va. (recipients)
events.description: Letter of thanks from Alexandria dated Feb. 13, 1865, to the Ladies of the Sanitary of St. Thomas' Church for 'Sanitaries' (supplies for sick and wounded soldiers) received Jan. 30; 'yours being the first colored society which has made us a donation of the kind.' Mentions the L'Ouverture general hospital and two branch hospitals in churches. Signature illegible on the film ('... Jacobs').

events.name: Donation visits for Rev. H. Davis at Rocky Hill and Princeton, N.J.
events.location: Bethel A.M.E., Rocky Hill, N.J.; Mount Pisgah A.M.E., Princeton, N.J.
events.description: Rocky Hill: $13.55 collected for the pastor (notice dated Feb. 7, 1865); members who got it up, as printed (faint): Mrs. D. O. C[...], Mrs. H. D. Cr[...], Mrs. R. O. Salters [VERIFY], Mrs. G. O. Ruddle [VERIFY]. Princeton: Female Itinerant Society refreshment table plus cash, total given $26.80 [VERIFY first digit] (cash to pastor $10.80); committee Mrs. M. H. Conover, Mrs. S. D. Rushman [VERIFY], Mrs. H. D. Hagerman, Mrs. C. D. Juel [VERIFY], Mrs. M. J. Conover. Both signed H. Davis, Pastor (Philadelphia Conference New Jersey work).

events.name: Good Samaritans District Grand Lodge No. 2 -- quarterly meeting called
events.location: new Masonic Hall, South Eleventh street, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly Meeting of the R. W. District Grand Lodge No. 2, Independent Order of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria (Pennsylvania and Delaware), 10 A.M. Lodges to be punctual with reports and dues. By order of R. H. Gleaves, R.W.G.Q. [title letters faint]; attest Jonathan Davis, M.D., R.W.G.R., Sec.

events.name: Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia -- fair for sick and wounded colored soldiers announced
