events.description: Standing appeal (dated 'Jan. 10.--2mo.') for money or goods for another fair, to open April 17 at Concert Hall. Officers: President Miss Amelia E. Mills, 1015 Lombard street; Vice President Mrs. Emma L. Jackson, 615 Clifton street; Treasurer Miss Rebecca Venning, 911 Rodman street; Secretary Miss S. Lizzie Brown, 913 South street; Cor. Secretary Miss S. Louisa Iredell, 917 Washington avenue. Committee: Mrs. David Bowers, 481 North Fourth St.; Mrs. Henry Johnson, 1106 Fitzwater; Mrs. Joseph Bustill, 403 South Sixth; Mrs. Thos. Davis, N. E. cor. 11th and Race; Mrs. R. M. Adger, 825 South St.; Mrs. Jas. Wilson, 907 Lombard St.; Mrs. A. Adams, 820 Juniper street.

events.name: J. Mercer Langston lectures on 'The War our Emancipator' (streetcar exclusion cited)
events.description: Fifth lecture of the Social, Civil and Statistical Association course. Langston (of Ohio) said that 'in this city of Philadelphia, this city of civilization, a man cannot ride in the street cars because the Lord has touched his cheek with a brush with a little black paint on it,' contrasting it with the tax-receiver who makes no distinction of color; he called for the ballot. STREETCAR topic. Date computed from 'last Thursday evening' before the Saturday Mar 18 issue.

events.name: Fifth and Sixth Street Passenger Railway Co. announces it will carry colored passengers
events.description: STREETCAR topic. Pvt. Henry Carpenter Hoyle, Co. F, 43d U.S.C.T. (a Camp William Penn regiment), writing from camp near Richmond Feb. 18, 1865, reports reading in the Philadelphia Inquirer 'a few days ago' an advertisement of the Fifth and Sixth Street Passenger Railway Company 'announcing their intention of allowing colored people to ride in the cars of their line,' calling it 'another progressive stride, which redounds to the credit of the Quaker City,' while protesting that soldiers are still kept from rights they fight for. Date of the Inquirer advertisement not given (before Feb. 18, 1865).
attendees: private, Co. F, 43d U.S.C.T. (reporter of the item)

events.name: Bethel Church Sabbath School Association sends box to freedpeople at Norfolk
events.description: Box of clothing, books and papers sent by the Committee of the Sabbath School Association of Bethel Church, Philadelphia, to S. L. Daffin, teacher among the freedpeople at Norfolk, Va., who acknowledged it on 21st 2d mo. 1865 ('Yours for the freed people'). Daffin (Sallie L. Daffin, Philadelphia teacher) not linked: the printed form gives initials only.

events.name: Princeton (Mount Pisgah A.M.E.) collection for Wilberforce University
events.location: Mount Pisgah A.M.E. Church, Princeton, N.J.
events.description: Rev. Henry Davis, Elder, $1.00, then about thirty contributors at $1.00 or 50 cents; total $21.05, plus a later collection of $3.95, making $25 forwarded to the Treasurer of Wilberforce College. Names clearly read: Harper Hagerman, James Schenck, Harriet Hagerman, Rachel Hagerman, Cornelia Conover, Julia Conover, Lydia Simpson, Harriet Schenck, Sarah A. Bookman, Richard A. Striker. Faint or partial (not linked): Whitefield Polemus [VERIFY], ... Schuyler [VERIFY], ... Vanzant, Sarah A. Onque [VERIFY], Nancy Hart [VERIFY], Amelia Jennings [VERIFY], Isaac Pidgeon [VERIFY], Margaret ..., Philip ..., Ellas [?] Conover, plus ten illegible lines (Joseph ..., Anna ..., etc.).

events.name: Philadelphia preachers' meeting at Bethel contributes to superannuated Rev. Holcomb
events.description: Preachers' meeting in Bethel Church 'on the 31st ult.' (as printed; February has no 31st, so the date is uncertain [VERIFY]) gave $6.50 for the Rev. [initial obscured] Holcomb, a worn-out father now 'afflicted in his cottage beside the wilderness'; delivered by T. Gould of Burlington, N.J., who urges the Philadelphia District not to forget the superannuated fathers.

events.name: Former residents of Charleston meet to aid Charleston sufferers
events.description: Meeting of former residents of Charleston, S.C., held in Philadelphia in February 1865 (day printed '2[?]'; report dated Feb. 26). Charles L. Ferrette, chair; R. M. Adger, secretary. Committee on resolutions: Joseph A. Lacombe, Theodore Smith and John [?] Wells [VERIFY]. Resolutions: pledge to aid the people of Charleston, solicit help, appeal through the papers to the public of Philadelphia and elsewhere; clothing and shoes much needed. Depots for donations: Bascom and Smith, 261 S. 8th St. (number and street confirmed on the Mar 25 reprint); Robert Adger, 821 South St.; J. A. Lacombe, 1002 Locust St.; Thaddeus Manning, 1410 South St.; Ashley Bascom, 735 S. 11th St. (confirmed on the Mar 25 reprint); Clifton Houston, at Wm. Still's, Fifth & Arch streets; and other gentlemen with books signed by the officers.

events.name: Bethel A.M.E. Sabbath School grand concert announced
events.description: Grand concert by the Sabbath School of Bethel A.M.E. Church with several well-known artists; tickets 25 cents, a few on sale at the Recorder office, 619 Pine street. The editor advises buying early 'to avoid the rush which generally attends the concerts given by this school.'

events.name: Hon. W. D. Kelley's lecture, closing the Social, Civil and Statistical Association course
events.description: Sixth and final lecture of the winter course ('The War, and the Rights of Humanity'); hall crowded. Singers Miss E. T. Greenfield, Miss Kate Laurier, Mr. W. Sturges and Count J. De Cliff; Post Band from Camp Wm. Penn. Mr. R. Purves introduced the lecturer, who spoke nearly two hours; Kelley said that in Massachusetts every man, white and colored, who can read the Constitution is a qualified voter. The paper hopes to print the Report of the Committee on Lectures of the S., C., and S. Association.

events.name: Two Black soldiers forced off a streetcar platform; a Black man beaten for carrying a 'Greeley is coming' placard
events.description: STREETCAR topic. Letter dated Philadelphia, March 22, 1865, signed Britton Lanier, citing the Press 'to-day': (1) two soldiers in United States uniform were 'forced from the front platform' of one of the city's street cars because of their color ('We have petitioned time and again for permission to ride inside, and now we are driven from the outside'); (2) within twenty-four hours an 'innocent and peaceable colored man' was beaten by rowdies for 'bearing aloft the announcement, Greeley is coming,' and Rev. J. Wheaton Smith, 'one of the most noted of the clergy of this city,' was attacked for offering aid. Mob violence near the cars counts in the streetcar topic (owner's 1864 ruling). Exact dates not stated (shortly before Mar 22). Rev. J. Wheaton Smith was a white Baptist minister; linked as the named victim.

events.name: Union League Association -- election of officers
events.description: Regular meeting 'held on Thursday evening, March 17th' (as printed; Thursday was March 16, 1865 [VERIFY date]). Officers: John C. Bowers, President; David B. Bowser and Jesse E. [or K.] Glasgow [VERIFY initial], Vice-Presidents; Joseph W. Cassey [VERIFY: second letter reads u or a] and Andrew F. Stevens, Secretaries; Rev. Stephen Smith, Treasurer; John H. Colbert, Thomas J. Bowers, Benjamin Harrison, Robert Adger, Sr., and Charles Simpson, Board of Directors. This is the Black Philadelphians' Union League Association (cf. Bowser, Bowers, Adger), not the white Union League Club.

notes: CR_1865-01-07: issue is Vol. V, No. 1, New Series (Whole No. 209). Four pages read in full.

p1: chaplain's diary of the fleet expedition off Wilmington (1st U.S.C.T. context; not Philadelphia), letter of James H. Payne, quartermaster sergeant 27th U.S.C.T., praising Sister Lydia Penny (wife of Thomas Penny, 'a native of Pennsylvania', of the 5th U.S.C.T.); Newport R. I. Maryland-emancipation celebration (George T. Downing, Wm. Dorsey etc.); Albany letter; Morristown letter; essays. All out of scope, text only.

p2: soldier's letter from camp near Bermuda Hundred signed Thomas B. W...ter (Webster?), Orderly Sergeant Co. I, 43d (?) U.S.C.T. (a Camp William Penn regiment) on equal pay; not shown to be a Philadelphian, not linked. Canada West letter (Chatham) and A. W. Wayman's tour letter (mentions Brother Winder at Zion Mission Church, Philadelphia, in revival; Brother Stanford's revival; a visit to Union Church, Philadelphia; Allentown, Bordentown, New Hope, Burlington NJ) left in text.
p2 Banneker report prints 'Mr. O. C. Catto' (clearly O. V. Catto, teacher at the ICY high school); recorded as printed.
p2 Presbyterian debt jubilee: 'Rev. Mr. Reeve, Pastor' is J. B. Reeve of Central Presbyterian (Lombard St.); 'Mr. Jones' and 'Mr. Glasco' surname-only, not linked.
p2 Bethel SS: 'Revs. Moore and Smith' surname-only, not linked.
p3 Masonic (Pennsylvania): 'Aaron P. Faucett' and 'Redman Faucett' as printed; Fairbank committee and SCSA notice print 'Redman Faucet'.
p3 Fairbank committee prints 'Rev. E. Nearer', almost certainly a misprint for Rev. E. Weaver; not linked.
p3 New Jersey Grand Lodge: Joshua Woodlin is presumably Rev. Joshua Woodlin of the Philadelphia Conference (Woodlin Society namesake). Only principal officers linked; rest in description (NJ).
p3 Equal Rights League officers: Geo. B. Vashon (Pittsburgh), Nesbit, Wright, Nelson, Williams, Arnett, Hughes, Murray, Douglass, Cooper, Butler, Barenger are outside Philadelphia: text only.

p3 ads: James O. Clark M.D. and Nathaniel L. Durham ads first appear this issue ('Jan 7'). Thos. J. Bowers coal, W. R. Decordover periodical depot and Mrs. C. E. Harding dry goods (dated Oct. 1864) may already have been captured from Q4 1864 issues: check for duplicates before loading.

Repeats NOT re-entered: Joseph Brister dentist; Mrs. M. Bennett herb doctress; Georgina Gleaves 633 Pine; Bustill wig makers 403 S. Sixth; Miss Mary Still notice; S. Shorter Hawkins fall and winter goods (615 Lombard); Wm. Still stove store 107 N. Fifth; Book Depository; Wm. H. Longfellow dentist (now printed No. 1136 Rodman); Jane Johnson and Ann Wear shrouding 618 S. Eighth; Mrs. H. S. Duterte; Thomas Charnock; James W. Brown dyeing; Mrs. M. U. (?) Gibbons intelligence office, Pine St. (Sept. 24 ad); Miss Jane Jobs boarding at Fairhaven N.J. (out of town); Jas. B.
